//: Machine profile: Mac mini — single source of truth. The bare git repo
referenced by remoteUrl lives ON this machine (see
docs/machine-setup.md for the `git init --bare` bootstrap).
remoteUrl is a plain LOCAL FILESYSTEM path, not the `mini:` ssh alias
the MacBook/Linux profiles use — because this profile runs ON the mini
itself, the bare repo is already local. Routing the mini's own
pull/push/watch traffic through ssh to itself would add an unnecessary
network hop (and an unnecessary reachability-precheck ssh probe) for no
benefit; a local path is also what this package's own test suite uses
for local bare-repo remotes, so this is the well-exercised path.
If the mini's bare repo ever moves to a separate external host (i.e.
the mini itself becomes a fallback-style client rather than the host),
switch remoteUrl to the ssh form instead, e.g.:
"remoteUrl": "that-other-host:~/memory-sync/pandora-memory.git"
(same scp-like syntax macbook.json/linux.example.json use for `mini:`).
repositorySubdir MUST be identical across every machine sharing this
remote — it is the ONLY thing that determines the remote tree path
(see toRepositoryRelativePath in src/memory-sync/config.ts: remote path
= path.posix.join(repositorySubdir, <syncPaths destination + relative
path>)). It used to be set to 'mac-mini' here and 'macbook' in
macbook.json — that made the two machines write to two separate
top-level trees in the same bare repo and never see each other's
pushes (a live cross-machine E2E test caught this: mini `pull` after a
MacBook `push` reported applied=0). Both profiles now use the same
'pandora' value. The 'profile' field below is a DIFFERENT, unrelated
setting — it only names this machine's LOCAL state directory
(queue/base/tmp under stateDir); it is safe for it to differ per
machine (and it does: 'mac-mini' here, 'macbook' there) precisely
because it never touches the remote.
syncPaths is a single directory entry covering the ENTIRE rootDir
(source '.'), so every file agent-memory-sync finds there is synced —
the real Claude Code memory directory holds ~236 flat .md files with no
daily/ or logs/ subdirectories; the previous syncPaths (a literal
'MEMORY.md' file plus nonexistent daily/logs directories) missed all of
them. destination is the non-'.' literal 'memory', not '.': a bare '.'
destination round-trips through push but is silently unmappable on
pull/restore (mapRemotePathToLocalAbsolute's directory-prefix match
needs a real path segment, not '.' — verified empirically, see the
implementer's task notes / git history for this fix). A single
directory root also naturally covers any future subdirectories without
further changes.
stateDir is set OUTSIDE rootDir (a separate ~/.agent-memory-sync tree,
not '<rootDir>/.agent-memory-sync/...'), which matters now that
syncPaths covers the whole rootDir: if stateDir stayed nested inside
rootDir, syncPaths' recursive walk would also pick up this tool's own
internal git working copies/queue/base snapshots and try to sync them
as if they were memory content. An absolute stateDir value overrides
the rootDir-relative default entirely (path.resolve treats an absolute
second argument as authoritative) — see resolveRunConfig() in
src/config/loader.ts.
Namespace divergence (read before copying this file to another machine):
Claude Code derives its per-project memory slug from the absolute path
of the project working directory, including the OS username. On the
mini the repo lives at /Users/lannguyensi/git/pandora, so Claude Code
stores memory under
~/.claude/projects/-Users-lannguyensi-git-pandora/memory — hence the
hardcoded rootDir below. On the MacBook the OS user differs (lan), so
the same repository checkout path pattern yields a DIFFERENT slug:
-Users-lan-git-pandora (see macbook.json). The two machines' local
memory directories are intentionally NOT named the same; only the
remote (repositorySubdir 'pandora') and the shared bare repo are
common ground.
rootDir/stateDir (and remoteUrl here) intentionally use resolved
absolute paths rather than '~': agent-memory-sync's config loader does
not perform shell-style tilde expansion (path.resolve('~/x') resolves
'~' as a literal path segment, not the home directory) — see
src/config/loader.ts resolveRunConfig(). Adjust the /Users/lannguyensi
prefix if you copy this profile to a machine with a different OS
username.
Activation: pass BOTH --config (this file) and the 'mac-mini' profile
argument, e.g. `agent-memory-sync run mac-mini --config profiles/mac-mini.json`.
The CLI's [profile] positional argument always defaults to 'default' and
overrides this file's 'profile' field when omitted, so state files
(queue/, base/, tmp/) land under the intended profile subdirectory only
if the positional argument is passed explicitly too. See docs/machine-setup.md.
Reminder (see docs/machine-setup.md / README.md #systemd-unit): `watch`
alone is not sufficient even on the mini if you also run it here for
local edit backup — pair it with a periodic `run --mode sync` job,
since `watch` never pulls.
